entries.label: A touching curve read as having two distinct roots
entries.description: Treats a curve that meets the x-axis at one point as having two different solutions.
entries.signal: The solution set given has two elements where the curve only touches.

refutation.text_md: You are reading roots off the graph, which is exactly what this method is.
Count the points where the curve MEETS the axis: touching at one point means one repeated root, so the solution set has a single element.
Two distinct roots need the curve to cross the axis twice — and that is the case where the discriminant is positive rather than zero.

entries.label: No meeting point read as "every x is a solution"
entries.description: When the curve does not meet the x-axis, concludes that every real number solves the equation, instead of none.
entries.signal: The solution set given is $\mathbb{R}$ although the curve does not meet the $x$-axis.

refutation.text_md: A root is a value of $x$ that makes $f(x) = 0$. On the graph it is a point where the curve sits exactly on the $x$-axis.
If the curve never meets the $x$-axis, no such point exists: no value of $x$ makes $f(x) = 0$.
So the solution set is empty, $\varnothing$. $\mathbb{R}$ would mean that every $x$ works, which is the opposite.

entries.label: Roots read off the numbers in the equation
entries.description: Takes numbers written in the equation (its coefficients) as its roots, instead of reading where the curve meets the x-axis.
entries.signal: The solution set is made of numbers taken from the equation itself.

refutation.text_md: The numbers written in the equation, its coefficients, describe the curve. They are not its roots.
A root is an $x$ that makes $f(x) = 0$: on the graph, the $x$-coordinate of a point where the curve meets the $x$-axis. Substituting a candidate tells you at once whether it is one.
Read the roots from the meeting points: two, one, or none. When the curve does not meet the axis, the solution set is $\varnothing$.

entries.label: Keeps the negative solution as an answer
entries.description: The student solves with the formula, gets two values of x, and gives the negative one (or both) as the answer without checking it against the situation.
entries.signal: Answers x = -2.59, or says the disk lands at both -2.59 and 116.55 meters.

refutation.text_md: You used the formula correctly and found both roots, $-2.59$ and $116.5465116$. The slip is treating a quadratic's two solutions as two answers to the question, when only one may fit the situation.
In the disk race, $x$ is the horizontal distance in meters from the player. A distance of $-2.59$ meters has no meaning here, so that value is refused.
The question asks where the disk falls. The root that fits is $x=\frac{-4.9-5.123}{-0.086}=116.5465116$ meters.
So the answer is not $-2.59$, and it is not both values. The disk lands about $116.55$ meters away.
Next time, after finding both solutions, ask what $x$ stands for in the problem. Cross out any value that cannot be that quantity, then round the one left to the place asked for.

entries.label: Sign of the discriminant misread
entries.description: Reports real roots when b² − 4ac < 0, or no roots when it is positive.
entries.signal: The stated number of roots contradicts the sign of the discriminant.

refutation.text_md: Computing the discriminant is exactly the right first move.
Its SIGN decides: positive gives two different real roots, zero gives one repeated root, negative gives none in $\mathbb{R}$.
A negative discriminant means the curve never meets the $x$-axis, so the solution set is $\varnothing$.
